audience.text: C++ developers building desktop, server, or embedded applications that require PDF document processing without external runtime dependencies.

capabilities.text: Open existing PDF files, including password-protected ones, and inspect page count, metadata, and encryption status.
capabilities.title: Open and inspect PDF documents

capabilities.text: Extract full-page text using TextAbsorber or render pages to PNG, JPEG, BMP, or TIFF images using dedicated devices.
capabilities.title: Extract text and images

capabilities.text: Apply AES-256, AES-128, RC4-128, or RC4-40 encryption with granular permissions, and sign documents with detached PKCS#7 signatures.
capabilities.title: Encrypt and sign documents

capabilities.text: Build documents with positioned text, tables, vector shapes, watermarks, annotations, and interactive AcroForm fields.
capabilities.title: Create PDF content from scratch

capabilities.text: Add and manipulate annotations (Highlight, Text, Link, Stamp, etc.) and AcroForm fields (TextBox, Checkbox, ComboBox, etc.).
capabilities.title: Manage annotations and forms

capabilities.text: Create hierarchical bookmark trees and define reusable named destinations for navigation.
capabilities.title: Support outlines and named destinations

capabilities.text: Read and write document info (title, author, subject, keywords, dates) and XMP metadata.
capabilities.title: Handle document metadata

capabilities.text: Access procedural wrappers like PdfConverter, PdfExtractor, PdfFileEditor, PdfFileStamp, and PdfBookmarkEditor.
capabilities.title: Use legacy facades API

limitations.text: Standard-14 font fallback covers 12 fonts (Helvetica, Times-Roman, Courier × 4 styles); Symbol and ZapfDingbats have no bundled fallback.
XmpValue type-checking helpers (IsDateTime, IsField, etc.) are stubs that always return false; use IsString/IsInteger/IsDouble/IsArray instead.
Setting metadata on a from-scratch document and saving throws because there is no existing /Info object to patch.
Permissions set via encryption are enforced by the consuming PDF viewer, not by the library itself — it is not a DRM mechanism.

problems_solved.text: Enables reading, writing, and modifying PDF documents in C++ without relying on commercial or third-party PDF libraries.
Provides text extraction, page rendering, and metadata handling through a consistent, object-oriented API aligned with Aspose.PDF for .NET.
Supports encryption, signing, annotations, and form fields for secure and interactive PDF workflows.
Delivers a self-contained implementation of PDF codecs (TIFF, JPEG, PNG) and rendering without external runtime dependencies.

product_summary.text: Aspose.PDF FOSS for C++ is a free, open-source C++20 library for creating, editing, and processing PDF documents with no runtime dependencies.

uncertainties: The exact set of supported AcroForm field types beyond those explicitly listed in examples and public symbols is unclear.
The behavior of TiffDevice for multi-page TIFF output beyond the documented Process(Document, startPage, endPage, ostream) overload is not specified.
Whether the library supports PDF/A or PDF/UA conformance beyond basic PDF 1.7/2.0 features is not stated in the facts.

workflows.name: Open and inspect PDF
workflows.text: Load a PDF file, check encryption status, and read document metadata such as title and author.

workflows.name: Extract content
workflows.text: Traverse pages to extract text using TextAbsorber or render pages to raster images using PngDevice, JpegDevice, or TiffDevice.

workflows.name: Encrypt and sign
workflows.text: Apply AES-256 or RC4 encryption with granular permissions, or sign documents using Facades::PdfFileSignature.

workflows.name: Build from scratch
workflows.text: Create new documents with text, tables, vector graphics, watermarks, annotations, and interactive form fields.

workflows.name: Use legacy facades
workflows.text: Leverage Facades such as PdfConverter, PdfExtractor, PdfFileSignature, PdfFileEditor, and PdfFileStamp for familiar procedural patterns.

workflows.name: Build and integrate
workflows.text: Build the library as a static library using CMake 3.20+ and link it into C++20 projects with no runtime dependencies.
